reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address thermal exposure, diffusion-driven phase evolution, high-temperature oxidation, or the specific mechanistic link between Mg mobility and property changes. E1 reports corrosion behavior and oxide film formation in as-synthesized Mg-Ti-Zn alloys, while E2 describes as-cast and heat-treated Al-based lightweight alloys but provides no data on Mg diffusion, oxide scale evolution, or corrosion kinetics under the proposed conditions. The key premises thus lack specific prior evidential support.
premises: Mg is highly mobile in non-equilibrium microstructures and diffuses upon thermal exposure
Mg diffusion leads to formation of Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates and matrix enrichment in passivating elements
Matrix enrichment in passivating elements promotes a protective, adherent oxide scale during high-temperature oxidation
